# Layouts

## Slide layouts 

* In a traditional slide presentation software like, [LibreOffice Impress](https://www.libreoffice.org/discover/impress/) or Powerpoint, there is the concept of slide layouts 


![Layouts](assets/img/powerpoint-slide-layout.png){height=50%}



* Layouts define the placement and structure of text or image components in the slide, and persist the layout even after theme changes


## Regular slide

To compose regular slides, use the syntax:

1. Section slides start a line with a single ++#++ (-w- and a space after the title --)
2. Regular slides start a line with double ++##++
3. Sub-blocks inside a slide start a line with ++###++
#. To split a slide without the title, start a line with @@---@@ 

## Frame attributes 

* In Quarto, it is possible to pass [attributes to a frame]{https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/beamer.html#frame-attributes}
* The syntax is: 

        ## Fit contents slides {.shrink}

NOTE: In this case the slide contents are shrinked to fit the frame

# Custom layouts provided by this package

## Custom layouts

* Some layouts are particularly used in presentations, like:
  * An all white or black slide to include an image
  * The same without title 
  * Slide without footer

* Some slide attributes, _frameoptions_ in Beamer nomenclature, can be passed to the slide title and modify its behavior

<!-- -->

::: {.admonitiontip}

The syntax is different, and we have to pass the attribute ++frameoptions=++ inside braces:

    ## Slide {frameoptions="<value>"}
:::

* In the following slides some of these new layouts are presented

## Black with title {frameoptions="black"}

A black background slide

    ## Black with title {frameoptions="black"}


## Black with title no footer {frameoptions="black,plain"}

A black background slide with a title and without footer

To remove the footer add the `plain` or `bare` option

    ## Blacktitle {frameoptions="black,plain"}

## Black WITHOUT title {frameoptions="black,notitle"}

A black background slide without the title and footer

To remove the footer add the `notitle` option

    ## Black with title {frameoptions="black,notitle"}

NOTE: The "notitle" option also works for normal slides

## blackplain: black WITHOUT title/footer {frameoptions="blackplain"}

A black background slide without the title and footer

    ## Black with title {frameoptions="blackplain"}

Is the same as:

    ## Black with title {frameoptions="black,plain,notitle"}


## Black slide notitle {frameoptions="black,bare"}

For an all black slide without title and footer:

    ## Black slide notitle {frameoptions="black,bare"}

Is the same as:

    ## Black slide {frameoption="blackplain"}


## White slide {frameoptions="white" }

All white slide syntax:

    ## {frameoption="white"}


## White slide { frameoptions="whiteplain" }

All white WITHOUT title

    ## White slide {frameoption="whiteplain"}

Is the same as:

    ## White slide {frameoption="white,notitle"}

## Summary of slide layouts

- Use the construct:

      ## Title {frameoption=""}


- The list of possible options are:

:::list-table

  * - frameoption
    - Background
    - Title
    - Footer

  * - black
    - Black
    - Yes
    - Yes

  * - blackplain or black,bare
    - Black
    - No
    - No

  * - black,notitle
    - Black
    - No
    - Yes

  * - black,nofoot
    - Black
    - Yes
    - No

  * - white
    - White
    - Yes
    - No

  * - whiteplain
    - White
    - No
    - No

:::

- The options "bare", "plain", "notitle" and "nofoot" can be used in any slide



# Dividing in columns 

## Layout implementation: two columns

* One of the most used layouts is the division of the slide in two columns 
* Quarto provides this using the [multi column Div syntax](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/beamer.html#multiple-columns)


```markdown
:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}
contents Left column...
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
contents Right column...
:::

::::
```
* Another alternative is the [Quarto Div layout syntax](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/figures.html#complex-layouts), which offers full layout customization

## Easier columns 

* This extension provides the [twocol class](https://github.com/gpappasunb/twocol) Div to easily create two columns 
    * With this Div, the two columns are separated by @@ - - - @@

### Markdown code

```md
::: {.twocol}
Left column text 

- - -
Right column contents

* Item 1

:::
```

### Rendered columns

::: {.twocol}
Left column text 

- - -
Right column contents

* Item 1

:::

# Flexible columns with class .split

## Two columns with the split class

* The `split` class offers a flexible way to create columns, using the LaTeX `tcolorbox` class
* Put the two columns inside a div with class ".split" and separate the columns with [* * *]{.hl} or [- - -]{.hl}, starting in the first column 
* The main advantage is that the user has finer control over the placement and styling of the contents

:::markdownrender

:::: {.split }
 
Content left
 
- - -

Content right
 
::::


:::

## split class with arguments

* The `split` class can have several arguments:

[.split with arguments]{.rule opts="Purple"}

    {.split title='Box title' style=split titleleft='Left column' titleright='Right column'}

::: {.split title="Box title" style=split titleleft="Left column" titleright="Right column"}
 
title
:  adds a title frame
 
style 
:  ++split++ will color the columns differently

<!-- -->

* * *

Content right
 
:::

<!-- ++{.split title='Box title' style=split titleleft='Left column' titleright='Right column'}++(scale=0.8) -->

---

[.split without title and different colors]{.ruletitled}

    {.split style=split bgleft=green!20 bgright=orange!35 }

::: {.split style=split bgleft=green!20 bgright=orange!35 }
 
Left content

* * *

Content right
 
:::

## Available arguments for split class {.shrink}

Arguments for the ++split++ class should follow its definition, and are space-separated


| Argument   | Description    |
|--------------- | --------------- |
| title     | Main title. If not provided no title frame is shown|
| align     | Exactly two values indicating text alignment in the column. align='center,right' | 
| ratio     | Width of the left-hand column. Value between 0 and 1 | 
| left or titleleft | Subtitle left of column  |
| right or titleright| Subtitle right of column |
| bgleft/bgright | Background color left/right|
| style     | Custom tcolorbox style for the box|
| image     | Path of image add to the right column | 
:  Possible values for split class arguments

## split with style

* The argument _style_ provides provides column customization using the options in: [T-F-S/tcolorbox: A LaTeX package to create highly customizable colored boxes.](https://github.com/T-F-S/tcolorbox)


::: {.split style="sidebyside,bicolor,colupper=red,fontupper={\\huge\\ttfamily},lefthand width=2.2cm,fontlower={\\tiny}" bgleft=green!20 bgright=Tomato!35 }
 
Left content

* * *

    ::: {.split 
    style="sidebyside,bicolor,colupper=red,fontlower={\\tiny}" 
    bgleft=green!20 
    bgright=orange!35}

style="sidebyside, bicolor, colupper=red, fontupper={\\\\huge\\\\ttfamily}, lefthand width=2.2cm, fontlower={\\\\tiny}"

:::

NOTE: The options "sidebyside,bicolor" are necessary to produce two columns and distinct colors. If not provided, the split class produces a two row box with a single color

## split with style, predefined styles


* Some styles are predefined

| style=   | Description    |
|--------------- | --------------- |
| split   | column height is full slide, different column colors   |
| splitblack   | same as split, right column is black   |
| splitblank   | same as split, all columns are white |
: Predefined styles available for the split class {.stripped}

---

## Styles can be reused

* The recommended style is `style=split`

:::::{.split style="split"}

Left contents

* * *

    {.split style="split"}

:::::

## Style splitblack

* An alternative is `splitblack`, which turns the right background black and adjusts the text color

:::::{.split style="splitblack"}

Left contents

* * *

    {.split style="splitblack"}

The text also changes color

:::::

## Style splitblank

:::::{.split style="splitblank"}

Left contents

* * *

    {.split style="splitblank"}

Right contents

:::::

## Styles can be reused

:::::{.split style="split,colupper=White,colback=DodgerBlue" ratio=0.2}

**Left contents**

* * *

    {.split style="split,colupper=White,colback=DodgerBlue" ratio=0.2}

::comment-dots::(fg=MyGreen)

 * split parameters are provided as space-separated key=value pairs
* The options for `style` are taken directly from [tcolorbox package][tcolorbox]
* `ratio=` is a parameter of the split class, and not a style option. It creates different column sizes, always referring to a ratio of the width of the _left_ column. In this case, the left column takes 0.2 (20%) of the width

:::::

## split horizontal

* It is possible to create an horizontal split, resulting in two rows instead of two columns


:::::{.split style=split horizontal=true ratio=0.35}

Left contents are on top now

--- Key option:--- 

++horizontal=true++

* * *

    {.split style=split horizontal=true}

:::::


# split class with images 


## Adding images to split 

* The `split` class accepts the `image` parameter 

      ::: {.split image=linux}
      Left content
      * * *
      Text before image
      :::
      
NOTE: Horizontal Rule marker (* * *) is mandatory, even without text before image

* The value is the image path. If the extension is [.png]{.monoblue}, the it can be omitted 
* The image is added to the **right** panel 
  * Regular content can also be added to the right panel
  * The image is always inserted at the right column 
  * Some text can be added to the image (after the separator). It appears, [before]{.it} the image 

## split with images

::: {.split style=splitimage image=linux}
 
      ::: {.split style=splitimage image=logo.png}
      
      Notice that the style is "splitimage" 
        for a white background

      * * *
      
      Text before image
        In the bottom put any text you want
      :::

* * *

Text before image
<!-- Notice that the Horizontal Rule marker is mandatory, even without contents -->
:::

# The sideimage class

## Using the sideimage environment

* To facilitate even more the inclusion of images, there is another class: ++.sideimage++
* The sideimage class accepts directly an image parameter 
  * The image is always added to the right panel 
  * The text inside the block is rendered to the left pane
  * There is no need to separate the column contents with @@- - -@@

<!-- -->

```markdown
::: {.sideimage image=linux}
Contents shown at the left column
:::

```

- - - 

::::markdownrender

::: {.sideimage image=linux}
 
Using the sideimage Div

- one
- two
- three

:::

::::

## Using the sideimage environment with a pause (animation)

::: {.sideimage image=linux animate=true}
```md
::: {.sideimage 
image=logo.png 
pause=true}
```

The option +!pause=true!+ animates the image, showing it after the text on the left
 
:::

## sideimage using a tcolorbox style

::: {.sideimage image=linux style=splitimage}
 
+! {.sideimage image=linux style=splitimage} !+


:::

## sideimage using a tcolorbox style

::: {.sideimage image=linux style=splitblack}
 
    {.sideimage image=linux style=splitblack}

!v 1cm v!

--- Options: ---

* The `style=splitblack` paints the image background in black


:::

## Sideimage, with image at the left side


::: {.sideimage image=linux swap=true}
 
 The syntax is simply:

    {.sideimage image=linux swap=true}

--- Key option: swap=true ---

:::

## Sideimage, with image at the bottom (instead of right)


::: {.sideimage image=linux horizontal=true style=splitimage scale=0.15}
 
 The syntax is simply:

    {.sideimage image=linux horizontal=true style=splitimage scale=0.15}

--- Key option: horizontal=true ---

::: {.atip}
`style=splitimage` creates boxes with full page height, with different colors

++scale=0.15++ Scales down the image. Maybe necessary in horizontal mode
:::

:::

## Sideimage, with image at the bottom and height set to 0.2 of the top part (20%)


::: {.sideimage image=linux horizontal=true style=splitimage ratio=0.2 scale=0.3}
 
 The syntax is:

+! {.sideimage image=linux horizontal=true style=splitimage ratio=0.2 scale=0.3} !+

:::


## Separating slide with horizontal rules

* Horizontal rules can be drawn to separate topics in the slide
* Use a span with the class `.hr` (horizontal rule)
  * The span contents can contain a text. It is presented centered in the line

### Use of hr span

```markdown
[text]{.hr}

[text]{.hr pass="color=orange,width=6pt,fg=blue,pos=left"}
```

### Rendered

[text]{.hr}

[text]{.hr pass="color=orange,width=6pt,fg=blue,pos=left"}


## Separating slide with horizontal rules (cont.) {.shrink}

* Several options can be passed to `hr` 

### Options 

* color: rule color
* width: rule width
* fg: text color 
* pos: left, right or center (default). Text placement
* Text is optional to the span element

### Shortcut markup

* `xxxx` Four x characters is a shortcut for an horizontal rule. Change this in the `flexspan` yml definition 

xxxx
    
    === Text ===    ->  Enclose text in 3 '=' 

=== Text ===

    === Text ===(color=orange!20,pos=right) ->  customize the rule

=== Text ===(color=orange!20,pos=right)

    === Attention! ==! : displays a **red** rule. The right placeholder is "==!"

=== Attention! ==!


## Titled rules

* Another type of separation is a titled rule. It can be rendered using the class `rule` 
<!-- -->

        [Titled section]{.rule}

[Titled section]{.rule}

* The only option available is the color 
<!-- -->

        [Titled section in red]{.rule opts="red"}

[Titled section in red]{.rule opts="red"}

* There is a simple shortcut notation. Enclose in '---'

<!-- -->

        --- Titled rule ---
--- Titled rule ---

* The color can be changed inside the parenthesis

<!-- -->

        --- Titled rule ---(Tomato)
--- Titled rule ---(Tomato)
